patch_description: The known optimal 14-point packing (ratio^2 = 1/4.165849767, i.e. ratio ≈ 0.4894... in linear terms of dmin/dmax? Actually the reference squared ratio is 1/4.165849767 ≈ 0.24004, matching the current 0.24) is believed to be antipodally symmetric (icosahedron-like plus poles arrangement). The recommendation from the analysis suggests adding a mirror/antipodal-symmetry refinement pass: after the SLSQP polishing of the best candidate, detect antipodal partner pairs via distance-matrix matching, average each point with the negation of its partner to enforce exact central symmetry, then run one short, tight SLSQP pass (maxiter 200, ftol 1e-16) from the symmetrized configuration. This restricts the search to the symmetric subspace where the optimum likely lies, potentially nudging the ratio above the current local optimum. We implement this as a final stage: match point i to point j minimizing |x_i + x_j|, symmetrize, polish, and keep the result only if it improves the ratio.
